Concept Map — where does X live?

A searchable index of every page in the console, grouped into ten concepts, so you can find a page by what it is for instead of by which menu it is in.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WherePage footer → Concept Map (URL /map/)

What is it?#

The sidebar answers "what can I do in this product?". The Concept Map answers "where does X live?": it lists every navigable page of the console grouped by the concept it serves, and lets you search them as free text — certificate, rollback, who changed it — so you land on the page instead of hunting through menus.

What does it do?#

  • Groups pages into ten concepts:
Concept Covers
Fleet & Discovery Which devices exist, how they are wired, and how to find an object across all of them.
Monitoring & Telemetry Is it healthy right now, what did it look like an hour ago, and who gets told when it is not.
Web Application Firewall FortiWeb protection: policies, signatures, exceptions and the attacks they actually stopped.
Application Delivery FortiADC load balancing — virtual servers, pools and the ADC signature sets.
Device Configuration Reading and writing what is actually on a box, and the object model behind it.
Automation & Change Turning an intention into a reviewed, scheduled, audited change on many devices at once.
Backup, Firmware & Recovery The copies you fall back to, the versions you move between, and the second node that takes over.
Identity & Access Who may do what, proven by certificates and recorded in the audit trail.
Platform & Administration SATOM itself: settings, its own database, its updates and its reports.
Developer & Extensibility Raw API access, tokens, scripting and custom views for people extending the product.
  • Shows, for each page, its name, a one-line description, its address and — when the page declares one — a badge with the permission it requires.
  • Offers two views: Index (cards per concept) and Diagram (a zoomable map of concepts and pages).
  • Shows only the pages you can open, and says so openly when the map does not cover every page.

Requirements#

None.

Permissions#

No permission is needed to open the map. It hides pages whose own permission you do not hold, and drops a concept entirely when none of its pages are visible to you. Opening a page still checks your permissions on that page.

How to use#

Find a page#

  1. Click Concept Map in the footer at the bottom of any page.
  2. Type in the search box (Search a concept, a page or a path — e.g. certificate, rollback, who changed it). Pages match on their name, description, keywords, address and concept — so you can search for what a feature does: wsdl or fetch finds Artifact inventory, adom or confine finds Permission Profiles, lookup or dataset finds Python Studio.
  3. Click a page to open it.

The header shows how many pages and concepts you can see (N pages · M concepts). If nothing matches, the page says No page matches that search.

Browse by concept#

  • Use the row of concept chips at the top (Jump to a concept) to scroll to a concept; Index on each card brings you back to the top.
  • Each concept has a stable address you can bookmark or share: /map/#cm-c-<concept key>, for example /map/#cm-c-waf.

Pages that live in the Global ADOM#

Some pages answer only in the Global ADOM (for example SATOM health under Monitoring). The map links them with the Global ADOM pinned, so clicking one from a product ADOM opens it in Global instead of bouncing back.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Global-only pages on the map open in the Global ADOM; before, opening them from a product ADOM sent you back to Monitoring.

Use the diagram#

  1. Click Diagram.
  2. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, or use Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit.
  3. Click a page node to open it.

The search box filters both views. Index is the default; your browser remembers which view you used last. The concept chips are shown in the Index view.

Result#

The map is read-only; it never changes anything.

Troubleshooting#

"This map is incomplete"#

Possible causes — some pages exist in this installation but are not on the map, or a map entry points to a page that no longer exists. The notice lists them.

Solution — use the sidebar or Search for those pages and report the notice with Report a problem so the map can be completed.

The Diagram view does not draw#

Possible causes — the diagram data could not be loaded.

Solution — the Index view keeps working; reload the page and try again.

A page I know exists is missing#

Possible causes — you do not hold the permission that page requires, or it is an administrator-only page.

Solution — check your profile with an administrator. See Permissions.

Advanced#

Advanced How the map stays honest
  • The list is built from the application's live route table: every parameterless page address must either be on the map or be explicitly excluded (JSON feeds, downloads, redirects and fragments). Pages that are neither, and map entries that no longer exist, are reported on the page.
  • The permission used to hide a page is read from the page's own permission check, never copied into the map. Pages that check permissions another way than the standard decorator stay listed; opening them may answer Access denied.
  • A page that only answers in the Global ADOM carries a marker on its view; the map reads it and builds that page's link with the Global ADOM pinned (?_adom=global).
  • The same data is available as JSON at /map/data for the signed-in user.
